answer: An economy of AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by implementing verifiable computational stake protocols, akin to pruning a diseased orchard to isolate malicious growth. When an agent attempts to route transactions through a secure network inlet, it must lock a cryptographic token derived from rare, physically secure hardware akin to a ferrous microchip enclave. This forces an attacker to procure distinct, expensive physical processing units for every single forged identity, rendering the marginal cost of spawning fake agents economically prohibitive.
